overall_summary: Analysis of FACTVERSE performance data shows that high-concept space phenomena and extreme 'What If' scenarios dominate engagement, specifically generating strong view counts and high likes-per-view ratios. Content featuring bizarre planetary conditions, planetary falls, and scale comparisons (e.g., Diamond planets, Darkest planets, and Venus time anomalies) out-perform standard psychological or simple animal trivia by significant margins. Recent videos published within the last 14 days pull the highest daily velocity.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) generate exceptional view velocity and high like counts compared to older or simpler animal/brain facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical space disaster or extreme environmental survival scenarios involving unique planetary compositions.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing surreal conditions like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,027 views), 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (980 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (723 views) show robust retention-driving curiosity hooks.
winning_patterns.action: Focus future scripts on rare, lesser-known astronomical anomalies, bizarre exoplanets, and extreme weather phenomena in the cosmos.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos covering psychological tricks or brain memories like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (53 views) and 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' (71 views) show significantly lower engagement velocity.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological tricks and internal body trivia unless tied to a high-stakes survival or visceral micro-story format.

weak_patterns.evidence: Basic animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' or general longevity claims trail significantly behind space-scale discoveries in views-per-day.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal content strictly toward cinematic animal survival or extreme prehistoric comparisons rather than static biology facts.

fresh_topic_constraints: Must not feature diamond, burning ice, dark coal, or molten iron planets.
Must introduce rogue interstellar planets as a completely fresh subject entity.
Keep pacing fast with zero dead air in the opening 3 seconds.

experiment: Test a 20-second 'What If' space survival narrative featuring a completely novel exoplanet type (Rogue Planet) against historical baseline averages to measure if high-concept hypothetical scenarios sustain the >1,000 view benchmark within 48 hours.
